source_text: Sequitur in oratione: adueniat regnum tuum. regnum etiam Dei repraesentari nobis petimus, sicuti et nomen eius ut in nobis sanctificetur postulamus. nam Deus quando non regnat, aut aput eum quando incipit quod et semper fuit et esse non desinit ? nostrum regnum petimus aduenire a Deo nobis repromissum, Christi sanguine et passione quaesitum, ut qui in saeculo ante seruiuimus postmodum Christo dominante regnemus, sicut ipse pollicetur et dicit: uenite, benedicti patris mei, percipite regnum quod uobis paratum est ab origine mundi. potest uero, fratres dilectissimi, et ipse Christus esse regnum Dei quem uenire cottidie cupimus, cuius aduentus ut cito nobis repraesentetur optamus. nam cum resurrectio ipse sit, quia in ipso resurgimus, sic et regnum Dei potest ipse intellegi, quia in illo regnaturi sumus. bene autem regnum Dei petimus id est regnum caeleste, quia est et terrestre regnum. sed qui renuntiauit iam saeculo maior est et honoribus eius et regno. et ideo qui se Deo et Christo dicat non terrena sed caelestia regna desiderat. continua autem oratione et prece opus est, ne excidamus de regno caelesti, sicut Iudaei quibus hoc primum promissum fuerat exciderunt Domino manifestante et probante. multi inquit, uenient ab oriente et occidente et recumbent cum Abraham et Isaac et Iacob in regno caelorum. filii autem regni expellen tur in tene bras exteriores: illic erit ploratio et stridor dentium. ostendit quia ante filii regni Iudaei erant, quando et filii Dei esse perseuerabant, postquam cessauit circa illos nomen paternum, cessauit et regnum. et ideo christiani qui in oratione appellare patrem Deum coepimus nos et ut regnum Dei nobis ueniat oramus.
thought_title: The coming of the kingdom of God
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the second petition of the Lord's Prayer, 'your kingdom come,' after having discussed the hallowing of God's name.
pass_a_gloss: It follows in [the] prayer: may come your kingdom. [the] kingdom also of God to be represented to us we ask, just as also [the] name of him that in us may be sanctified we request. for God when [does he] not reign, or with him when does it begin that which both always was and to be [does] not cease? our kingdom we ask to come from God to us promised, by [the] blood of Christ and [the] passion sought, that [we] who in [the] world before served afterwards [with] Christ ruling may reign, just as he himself promises and says: come, blessed [ones] of my father, receive [the] kingdom which for you has been prepared from [the] origin of [the] world. [he] can [it] truly, brothers most beloved, also Christ himself [be] [the] kingdom of God whom to come daily we desire, whose coming that quickly to us may be represented we long for. for since [the] resurrection he himself is, because in him we rise again, so also [the] kingdom of God can he himself be understood, because in him we are going to reign. well moreover [the] kingdom of God we ask that is [the] kingdom heavenly, because there is also [a] earthly kingdom. but [he] who has renounced already [the] world greater is both [than] honors of it and [than its] kingdom. and therefore [he] who [dedicates] himself to God and to Christ not earthly but heavenly kingdoms desires. [there is] need moreover [of] continual prayer and supplication, lest we fall out of [the] kingdom heavenly, just as [the] Jews to whom this first had been promised fell out [with the] Lord showing and proving. many he says, will come from [the] east and [the] west and will recline with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in [the] kingdom of [the] heavens. [the] sons however of [the] kingdom will be expelled into [the] darkness outer: there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. he shows that before [the] sons of [the] kingdom [the] Jews were, when also [the] sons of God they were continuing to be, after ceased around them [the] name fatherly, ceased also [the] kingdom. and therefore [we] Christians who in prayer to call [upon] father God have begun [we] also that [the] kingdom of God to us may come pray.

lemmas.gloss: we may fall away, fall out

choices.why: The petition is quoted from the Lord's Prayer; the subjunctive 'adueniat' is a wish or petition, rendered with the bare subjunctive 'come' as in traditional English prayer language.
rejected: may your kingdom come
let your kingdom come

choices.english: we ask that the kingdom of God also be represented to us
choices.why: 'Repraesentari' means to be made present or brought before us; the passive infinitive after 'petimus' is rendered as a that-clause to keep the force of the request.
rejected: we ask the kingdom of God to be shown to us
we petition that the kingdom of God be presented to us

choices.english: sought by the blood and passion of Christ
choices.why: 'Quaesitum' is a perfect passive participle modifying 'regnum'; 'sought' preserves the idea of acquisition through Christ's suffering, not merely 'obtained.'
rejected: obtained by the blood and passion of Christ
won by the blood and passion of Christ

choices.term: ut qui in saeculo ante seruiuimus postmodum Christo dominante regnemus
choices.english: so that we who before served in the world may afterwards reign with Christ ruling
choices.why: 'Seruiuimus' means 'we served' or 'we were slaves'; 'Christo dominante' is an ablative absolute meaning 'with Christ ruling' or 'while Christ rules,' kept as a participial phrase to preserve the Latin construction.
rejected: so that we who were slaves in the world may afterwards reign under Christ's rule
so that we who served the world before may later reign when Christ rules

choices.term: uenite, benedicti patris mei, percipite regnum
choices.english: come, blessed of my Father, receive the kingdom
choices.why: The quotation from Matthew 25:34 is rendered literally; 'benedicti patris mei' is a genitive of source, 'blessed of my Father,' and 'percipite' is an imperative meaning 'receive' or 'take possession of.'
rejected: come, you who are blessed by my Father, inherit the kingdom
come, blessed ones of my Father, take the kingdom

choices.term: potest uero, fratres dilectissimi, et ipse Christus esse regnum Dei
choices.english: But truly, most beloved brothers, Christ himself can also be the kingdom of God
choices.why: 'Fratres dilectissimi' is Cyprian's characteristic address, rendered 'most beloved brothers'; 'potest...esse' is 'can be,' and 'et ipse Christus' is 'Christ himself also.'
rejected: indeed, dearest brothers, Christ himself can be the kingdom of God
but, most dear brothers, Christ himself can also be the kingdom of God

choices.term: cuius aduentus ut cito nobis repraesentetur optamus
choices.english: whose coming we long to be represented to us quickly
choices.why: 'Optamus' means 'we long for' or 'we wish'; the ut-clause with subjunctive 'repraesentetur' is a purpose or content clause after 'optamus,' rendered as an infinitive clause in English.
rejected: whose coming we desire to be shown to us soon
whose arrival we hope may be made present to us quickly

choices.english: because in him we are going to reign
choices.why: 'Regnaturi sumus' is a future periphrastic, 'we are going to reign' or 'we shall reign'; the future sense is important because it points to the eschatological reign.
rejected: because in him we shall reign
because we are to reign in him

choices.term: qui se Deo et Christo dicat
choices.english: he who dedicates himself to God and Christ
choices.why: 'Dicat' is from 'dico, dicare' meaning 'to dedicate, consecrate,' not 'dicere' meaning 'to say'; the subjunctive is generic, 'he who dedicates himself.'
rejected: he who says he belongs to God and Christ
he who devotes himself to God and Christ

choices.english: lest we fall away from the heavenly kingdom
choices.why: 'Excidamus' means 'we may fall out' or 'fall away'; the ne-clause is a negative purpose clause, rendered 'lest we fall away.'
rejected: so that we do not fall out of the heavenly kingdom
that we may not be cast out of the heavenly kingdom

choices.term: filii autem regni expellentur in tenebras exteriores
choices.english: But the children of the kingdom will be cast out into outer darkness
choices.why: The quotation from Matthew 8:12 is rendered literally; 'filii regni' is 'children of the kingdom,' and 'expellentur' is future passive, 'will be cast out.'
rejected: but the sons of the kingdom will be thrown into the outer darkness
but the children of the kingdom will be expelled into outer darkness

choices.term: postquam cessauit circa illos nomen paternum, cessauit et regnum
choices.english: after the fatherly name ceased among them, the kingdom also ceased
choices.why: 'Nomen paternum' is 'the fatherly name,' referring to their status as children of God; 'cessauit' is perfect, 'ceased,' and the parallel structure is preserved.
rejected: after the name of Father ceased for them, the kingdom also ceased
when the paternal name stopped among them, the kingdom also stopped

pass_b_english: The prayer continues: your kingdom come. We ask that the kingdom of God also be brought near to us, just as we ask that his name be hallowed in us. For when does God not reign, or when does that begin with him which always was and never ceases to be? We ask that our kingdom come, the kingdom promised to us by God, won by the blood and passion of Christ, so that we who before served in the world may afterwards reign with Christ ruling, as he himself promises and says: come, blessed of my Father, receive the kingdom prepared for you from the origin of the world (Matthew 25:34). But truly, most beloved brothers, Christ himself can also be the kingdom of God, whom we desire to come daily, whose coming we long to have brought near to us quickly. For since he himself is the resurrection, because in him we rise again, so also he himself can be understood as the kingdom of God, because in him we are going to reign. And we do well to ask for the kingdom of God, that is, the heavenly kingdom, because there is also an earthly kingdom. But he who has already renounced the world is greater than its honors and its kingdom. And therefore he who dedicates himself to God and Christ desires not earthly but heavenly kingdoms. But we need constant prayer and petition, lest we fall away from the heavenly kingdom, just as the Jews, to whom this was first promised, fell away, as the Lord shows and proves. Many, he says, will come from east and west and will recline with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven. But the children of the kingdom will be cast out into outer darkness: there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth (Matthew 8:11-12). He shows that the Jews were formerly children of the kingdom, when they also continued to be children of God. After the fatherly name ceased among them, the kingdom also ceased. And therefore we Christians, who have begun to call God Father in prayer, also pray that the kingdom of God may come to us.

problems.why: "repraesentari" means to be brought near/presented, not "represented" (made present vs symbolized).
problems.fix: brought near to us / made present to us

problems.quote: whose coming we long to be represented to us quickly
problems.source_quote: cuius aduentus ut cito nobis repraesentetur optamus
problems.why: Same error: "repraesentetur" means brought near/made present, not "represented"; awkward and wrong.
problems.fix: whose coming we long to have brought near to us quickly
problems.ruling: repraesentetur means 'be made present/brought near,' not 'represented'; meaning changed, reader misled.

problems.quote: the kingdom of God can be understood as himself
problems.why: "ipse" is the subject: "he himself can be understood as the kingdom of God," not kingdom understood as him.
problems.fix: he himself can be understood as the kingdom of God
problems.ruling: ipse is subject: 'he himself can be understood [as] the kingdom of God,' not 'kingdom understood as himself.' Meaning reversed.

edits.old: We ask that the kingdom of God also be represented to us
edits.new: We ask that the kingdom of God also be brought near to us

edits.old: whose coming we long to be represented to us quickly
edits.new: whose coming we long to have brought near to us quickly

edits.old: the kingdom of God can be understood as himself

fixed: Changed 'represented to us' to 'brought near to us' for 'repraesentari nobis' (made present, not symbolized).
Changed 'whose coming we long to be represented to us quickly' to 'whose coming we long to have brought near to us quickly' for 'cuius aduentus ut cito nobis repraesentetur optamus'.
Changed 'the kingdom of God can be understood as himself' to 'he himself can be understood as the kingdom of God' for 'regnum Dei potest ipse intellegi' (ipse is the subject).

problems.quote: sought by the blood and passion of Christ
problems.why: quaesitum means 'won/acquired for us,' not 'sought'; Christ's blood obtained the kingdom, didn't seek it.
problems.fix: won by the blood and passion of Christ
problems.ruling: quaesitum means 'obtained/won/acquired,' not 'sought'; Christ's blood acquired the kingdom, not sought it.

edits.old: sought by the blood and passion of Christ
edits.new: won by the blood and passion of Christ

last_rejected.quote: won by the blood and passion of Christ
last_rejected.why: "Quaesitum" means sought/acquired, not "won"; "passion" should be "suffering" or kept as "passion" in theological sense, but "won" misrepresents the acquisition through Christ's self-giving death.
last_rejected.fix: acquired by the blood and passion of Christ
last_rejected.ruling: Quaesitum can mean 'acquired/won'; 'passion' is standard for passio. No meaning lost.

last_rejected.why: "Christo dominante" is ablative absolute (Christ reigning/ruling), not "with Christ ruling" as accompaniment; it means "under Christ's lordship" or "when Christ rules."
last_rejected.ruling: 'With Christ ruling' correctly renders ablative absolute Christo dominante; standard English idiom.

last_rejected.quote: he who dedicates himself to God and Christ
last_rejected.source_quote: qui se Deo et Christo dicat
last_rejected.why: "Dicat" means "consecrates/devotes" (from "dicare"), not "dedicates" in the modern sense; more importantly, "dicat" is subjunctive in a relative clause of characteristic, "one who would consecrate himself."
last_rejected.fix: whoever would consecrate himself to God and Christ
last_rejected.ruling: Dicare means 'dedicate/consecrate'; 'dedicates' is within range. Subjunctive nuance not a major error.
